paper_metadata.title: Experimental Demonstration of Fermionic QAOA with One-Dimensional Cyclic Driver Hamiltonian

summary: The paper experimentally demonstrates a fermionic QAOA with a cyclic driver Hamiltonian on a 16‑qubit IonQ Aria trapped‑ion device for a portfolio optimization problem (N=8, D=2). The cyclic mixer reduces mixer gate complexity from O(N²D) to O(ND) and improves hardware performance: at p=1 the QPU achieves ΔE/W = 0.23±0.16 versus 0.34±0.17 for the previous ladder‑lattice FQAOA, with ≈0.17 probability of satisfying the fermion‑number constraint. The work shows noise reduction rather than computational advantage.

experiments.description: Fermionic QAOA (FQAOA) for portfolio optimization using the proposed one-dimensional cyclic driver Hamiltonian, evaluated by noiseless simulation and trapped-ion QPU experiment at p=1, compared against the previous ladder-lattice FQAOA and XY-QAOA baseline.

algorithm.variant: fermionic QAOA (FQAOA) with one-dimensional cyclic driver Hamiltonian
algorithm.parameter_initialization: QAA-inspired initial angles from discretized schedule: gamma_j^(0)=(2j-1)/(2p) * Δt, beta_j^(0)=(1-(2j-1)/(2p)) * Δt

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Unary fermionic encoding with one binary occupation variable x_{l,d} mapped to each fermionic mode n_{l,d}; total modes ND=16 for N=8, D=2.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize portfolio optimization Hamiltonian H_p = λ/K^2 * sum_{l,l'} sigma_{l,l'} sum_{d,d'} (n_{l,d}-1/2)(n_{l',d'}-1/2) + (1-λ)/K * sum_l mu_l sum_d (n_{l,d}-1/2) subject to total particle number C = sum_{l,d} n_{l,d} = M.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard constraint via fermion-number-conserving FQAOA mixer; post-selection on measurement outcomes satisfying M=4; debiasing error mitigation applied before post-selection.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_p as given in Eq. (15); constraint operator C = sum_{l=1}^N sum_{d=1}^D n_{l,d}

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization instance from prior studies, with N=8 assets and D=2 unary levels per asset; constraint K=4 holdings, corresponding to M=4 fermions.

dataset_specification.description: Covariance matrix sigma_{l,l'} and expected returns mu_l taken from Fig. 2 and Table IV of Ref. [2]; lambda=0.9; N=8, D=2, K=4.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Noiseless simulation with fixed-angle and optimized parameters; QPU experiment with 10,000 measurements and debiasing; post-selection on samples satisfying the particle-number constraint; comparison against random-with-constraint and ladder-lattice/XY-QAOA baselines.

noise_model.mitigation_details: Debiasing applied to 10,000 measurements; post-selection on M=4 samples; sharpening not applied.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Parameters initialized from QAA schedule; hopping integral t set by energy-scale ratio t=W/W_hop^alpha.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Debiasing, then post-selection on constraint-satisfying bitstrings; energy histograms and expectation values computed from selected samples.

speedup_claims.factor: O(ND) mixer gate operations vs O(N^2D) for previous ladder-lattice implementation
speedup_claims.conditions: for the cyclic driver Hamiltonian implementation of the mixer
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a gate-count reduction, not a proven runtime speedup; full ansatz gate counts still include the problem unitary and initial-state preparation.

speedup_claims.factor: about 2.5x improvement in probability of obtaining low-cost solutions
speedup_claims.conditions: trapped-ion QPU experiment at p=1 with debiasing and post-selection
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this in the summary; the detailed figure shows cyc-FQAOA peak probability around 0.25 versus about 0.10 for lad-FQAOA in the lowest-energy bin.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(ND) gate operations for the cyclic mixer; paper states mixer gate count reduced from O(N^2D) to O(ND)
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: For p-layer FQAOA, reported gate counts for cyclic mixer: single-qubit 388 + 232p, two-qubit 96 + 272p; at p=1 this gives 620 single-qubit and 368 two-qubit gates for the full ansatz as reported in the discussion.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unknown; the paper studies only a 16‑qubit instance (N=8, D=2) and does not estimate scaling to larger portfolios.
limiting_factors: Very small problem size (16 qubits, 8 assets)
Shallow circuit depth (p=1) required due to hardware noise
No comparison against strong classical portfolio optimizers
Performance gain limited to reduced gate count and noise sensitivity
Constraint violations increase rapidly with circuit depth

notes: Hardware is explicitly stated as IonQ Aria on Amazon Braket.
Num qubits inferred from N=8 and D=2 unary encoding, giving ND=16 physical qubits/modes.
Circuit depth reported as p=1 for the experiment; no transpiled depth given.
Speedup order is not claimed; only gate-count reduction and noise reduction are discussed.
Total gate counts are taken from the text comparing cyclic and ladder implementations; the paper reports counts as functions of p rather than a single compiled depth.
The authors do not claim quantum advantage; they claim reduced gate count and improved noise robustness versus ladder‑lattice FQAOA.
The only baseline with classical relevance is random sampling under the constraint; no competitive classical optimizer is benchmarked.
